definition: Requisition means a formal demand for goods or property made by an authority.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word requisition. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know requisition should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: A requisition arrived by motorcycle at dawn: every ferry on the lake now answered to the army.
A request is far weaker than a requisition — it leaves the choice on your side of the counter, and no is a complete answer; a requisition wears the same polite manners and takes the choice away.
Confiscation goes further than requisition — a requisition takes your trucks against a receipt and a rate; confiscation takes them and calls them the state's.

A seizure simply takes the thing — the trucks are gone, and no paper changes hands. A requisition is the documented demand: the authority names the goods, leaves a receipt, and often sets a rate. Both end with the state holding your property; only the requisition files the paperwork.

A levy is a demand measured out in money or men — a tax to pay, a quota of recruits to send, counted rather than named. A requisition points at the goods themselves: these ferries, that empty warehouse, the trucks in your yard. Authority demands both; they differ in what is counted.
